title: A nonzero section with a zero has positive degree on a proper integral curve
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $C$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_C$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], and let $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal L)$ be a nonzero global section. Then $\deg_k(\mathcal L)\ge0$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. If $s$ vanishes at some point of $C$, that is, if its nonvanishing locus $C_s$ of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module] is not all of $C$, then $\deg_k(\mathcal L)>0$.

source.place: Tag 0B40, lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial, clauses (1) and (2), with curve meaning integral separated finite type of dimension one.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the forward direction of the 0B5X argument a section of a power has a zero because the proper curve is not affine; 0B40 then gives strict positivity.
